vocab.example: All of economics is based on belief in the universality of the profit motive.
vocab.def: universal（普遍的）的名詞。這裡指「每個人都想賺錢」這件事放諸四海皆準。
vocab.exzh: 整個經濟學都建立在對獲利動機普遍性的信念上。

vocab.example: the profit motive makes people work harder and risk their capital.
vocab.def: 人們為了賺錢而行動的動力。資本主義就是靠它運轉的。
vocab.exzh: 獲利動機讓人們更努力工作，並且甘冒資本損失的風險。

vocab.example: The pursuit of profit has produced much of the material progress the world has enjoyed.
vocab.def: the pursuit of profit 是「追求利潤」。課文後面的 in some pursuits 則指「在某些競爭領域裡」，同一個字有兩種意思。
vocab.exzh: 對利潤的追求，創造了世界所享有的大部分物質進步。

vocab.example: In some pursuits, getting to the front of the pack means more schooling, more time in the gym or the library, better nutrition, more perspiration, greater stamina or better equipment.
vocab.def: 長時間維持體力或精力的能力。作者列出運動、讀書時靠努力就能勝出的條件，投資卻不是這樣。
vocab.exzh: 在某些領域，要擠進領先群，意味著更多的學習、花更多時間在健身房或圖書館、更好的營養、更多的汗水、更強的耐力或更好的裝備。

vocab.example: it calls for more perceptive thinking … at what I call the second level.
vocab.def: 能看出別人沒注意到的細節或道理。perceptive thinking 就是更有洞察力的思考。
vocab.exzh: 它需要更敏銳的思考……也就是我所稱的第二層。

vocab.example: Would-be investors can take courses in finance and accounting, read widely and, if they are fortunate, receive mentoring from someone with a deep understanding of the investment process.
vocab.def: 放在名詞前面，表示「想當、但還沒成為」。would-be investors 是想成為投資人的人。
vocab.exzh: 想成為投資人的人可以修金融與會計課程、廣泛閱讀，而且如果夠幸運，還能得到對投資流程有深刻理解的人指導。

vocab.example: Since other investors may be smart, well-informed and highly computerized, you must find an edge they don’t have.
vocab.def: 在競爭中比別人多出來的一點點優勢。find an edge 是投資人常說的話。
vocab.exzh: 既然其他投資人可能聰明、資訊靈通，而且高度電腦化，你就必須找到他們所沒有的優勢。

vocab.example: In short, being right may be a necessary condition for investment success, but it won’t be sufficient.
vocab.def: 與 necessary（必要的）搭配：necessary condition 是少了不行，sufficient 則是有了就夠。作者說「對」是必要，但不充分。
vocab.exzh: 簡單說，做對也許是投資成功的必要條件，但並不充分。

vocab.example: You must be more right than others … which by definition means your thinking has to be different.
vocab.def: 表示「從概念本身就必然成立」，不需要再證明。
vocab.exzh: 你必須比別人更正確……而依定義，這意味著你的想法必須與眾不同。

vocab.example: So the stock’s overrated and overpriced; let’s sell.
vocab.def: 大家給的評價高過實際價值。第二層思考者的重點，就是發現市場看法與事實之間的落差。
vocab.exzh: 所以這檔股票被高估，價格也太高了，賣掉吧。

vocab.example: The outlook calls for low growth and rising inflation. Let’s dump our stocks.
vocab.def: 口語用字，帶有急著脫手、不計價錢的味道。dump stocks 就是把股票全拋掉。
vocab.exzh: 前景看起來是低成長與通膨上升，我們把股票都拋掉吧。

vocab.example: First-level thinking is simplistic and superficial, and just about everyone can do it (a bad sign for anything involving an attempt at superiority).
vocab.def: 帶貶義，指把複雜的事看得太簡單。和 simple（簡單）不同，simple 是中性的。
vocab.exzh: 第一層思考過於簡化又流於表面，幾乎每個人都做得到（對任何想要出類拔萃的事來說，這是個壞跡象）。

vocab.example: First-level thinking is simplistic and superficial, and just about everyone can do it (a bad sign for anything involving an attempt at superiority).
vocab.def: 只看到表層、沒有深入理解。與 deep 相對。
vocab.exzh: 第一層思考過於簡化又流於表面，幾乎每個人都做得到（對任何想要出類拔萃的事來說，這是個壞跡象）。

sentences.en: Everyone wants to make money.
sentences.zh: 每個人都想賺錢。

sentences.en: All of economics is based on belief in the universality of the profit motive.
sentences.zh: 整個經濟學都建立在對獲利動機普遍性的信念上。

sentences.en: So is capitalism;
sentences.zh: 資本主義也是如此；

sentences.en: the profit motive makes people work harder and risk their capital.
sentences.zh: 獲利動機讓人們更努力工作，並且甘冒資本損失的風險。

sentences.en: The pursuit of profit has produced much of the material progress the world has enjoyed.
sentences.zh: 對利潤的追求，創造了世界所享有的大部分物質進步。

sentences.en: But that universality also makes beating the market a difficult task.
sentences.zh: 但這種普遍性也讓勝過市場成為一項困難的任務。

sentences.en: Millions of people are competing for each available dollar of investment gain.
sentences.zh: 有數百萬人在爭奪每一塊錢的投資獲利。

sentences.en: Who’ll get it?
sentences.zh: 誰會拿到？

sentences.en: The person who’s a step ahead.
sentences.zh: 是領先一步的那個人。

sentences.en: In some pursuits, getting to the front of the pack means more schooling, more time in the gym or the library, better nutrition, more perspiration, greater stamina or better equipment.
sentences.zh: 在某些領域，要擠進領先群，意味著更多的學習、花更多時間在健身房或圖書館、更好的營養、更多的汗水、更強的耐力或更好的裝備。

sentences.en: But in investing, where these things count for less, it calls for more perceptive thinking … at what I call the second level.
sentences.zh: 但在投資這一行，這些東西的作用比較小，它需要更敏銳的思考……也就是我所稱的第二層。

sentences.en: Would-be investors can take courses in finance and accounting, read widely and, if they are fortunate, receive mentoring from someone with a deep understanding of the investment process.
sentences.zh: 想成為投資人的人可以修金融與會計課程、廣泛閱讀，而且如果夠幸運，還能得到對投資流程有深刻理解的人指導。

sentences.en: But only a few of them will achieve the superior insight, intuition, sense of value and awareness of psychology that are required for consistently above-average results.
sentences.zh: 但其中只有少數人，能培養出始終取得高於平均成績所需要的卓越洞察力、直覺、價值感，以及對心理的警覺。

sentences.en: Doing so requires second-level thinking.
sentences.zh: 要做到這一點，需要第二層思考。

sentences.en: Remember, your goal in investing isn’t to earn average returns;
sentences.zh: 記住，你投資的目標不是賺到平均報酬；

sentences.en: you want to do better than average.
sentences.zh: 你要做得比平均更好。

sentences.en: Thus, your thinking has to be better than that of others—both more powerful and at a higher level.
sentences.zh: 因此，你的思考必須比別人更好——既更有力，層次也更高。

sentences.en: Since other investors may be smart, well-informed and highly computerized, you must find an edge they don’t have.
sentences.zh: 既然其他投資人可能聰明、資訊靈通，而且高度電腦化，你就必須找到他們所沒有的優勢。

sentences.en: You must think of something they haven’t thought of, see things they miss or bring insight they don’t possess.
sentences.zh: 你必須想到他們沒想到的事，看到他們錯過的東西，或帶來他們不具備的洞察。

sentences.en: You have to react differently and behave differently.
sentences.zh: 你必須有不同的反應，也有不同的行為。

sentences.en: In short, being right may be a necessary condition for investment success, but it won’t be sufficient.
sentences.zh: 簡單說，做對也許是投資成功的必要條件，但並不充分。

sentences.en: You must be more right than others … which by definition means your thinking has to be different.
sentences.zh: 你必須比別人更正確……而依定義，這意味著你的想法必須與眾不同。

sentences.en: What is second-level thinking?
sentences.zh: 什麼是第二層思考？

sentences.en: First-level thinking says, “It’s a good company; let’s buy the stock.”
sentences.zh: 第一層思考會說：「這是家好公司，我們買這檔股票吧。」

sentences.en: Second-level thinking says, “It’s a good company, but everyone thinks it’s a great company, and it’s not. So the stock’s overrated and overpriced; let’s sell.”
sentences.zh: 第二層思考會說：「這是家好公司，但是每個人都認為它是家偉大的公司，而它並不是。所以這檔股票被高估，價格也太高了，賣掉吧。」

sentences.en: First-level thinking says, “The outlook calls for low growth and rising inflation. Let’s dump our stocks.”
sentences.zh: 第一層思考會說：「前景看起來是低成長與通膨上升，我們把股票都拋掉吧。」

sentences.en: Second-level thinking says, “The outlook stinks, but everyone else is selling in panic. Buy!”
sentences.zh: 第二層思考會說：「前景糟透了，但其他人都在恐慌地賣出。買進！」

sentences.en: First-level thinking says, “I think the company’s earnings will fall; sell.”
sentences.zh: 第一層思考會說：「我認為這家公司的盈餘會下滑，賣出。」

sentences.en: Second-level thinking says, “I think the company’s earnings will fall less than people expect, and the pleasant surprise will lift the stock; buy.”
sentences.zh: 第二層思考會說：「我認為這家公司盈餘下滑的幅度會小於大家的預期，而這個令人愉快的驚喜會推升股價，買進。」

sentences.en: First-level thinking is simplistic and superficial, and just about everyone can do it (a bad sign for anything involving an attempt at superiority).
sentences.zh: 第一層思考過於簡化又流於表面，幾乎每個人都做得到（對任何想要出類拔萃的事來說，這是個壞跡象）。

sentences.en: All the first-level thinker needs is an opinion about the future, as in “The outlook for the company is favorable, meaning the stock will go up.”
sentences.zh: 第一層思考者所需要的，只是對未來的一個看法，比如：「這家公司的前景看好，意味著股價會上漲。」

grammar.point: So is capitalism：so ＋ be ＋ 主詞的倒裝
grammar.quote: All of economics is based on belief in the universality of the profit motive. So is capitalism
grammar.explain:
So ＋ be／助動詞 ＋ 主詞，意思是「…也是如此」，用來附和前一句的肯定句。這裡前面是 is based on…，所以用 So is。
如果前句是一般動詞，就改用 do／does／did：She likes it. So do I. 整句的意思是：資本主義也建立在對獲利動機普遍性的信念上。

grammar.point: 並列動詞中夾著條件插入語
grammar.quote: Would-be investors can take courses in finance and accounting, read widely and, if they are fortunate, receive mentoring from someone with a deep understanding of the investment process.
grammar.explain:
主詞 Would-be investors 後面有三個並列動詞：take、read、receive，共用助動詞 can。
if they are fortunate 是夾在 and 與 receive 之間的插入語，表示「如果夠幸運」。讀長句的訣竅是先把插入語拿掉，找出並列的骨架：can take…, read… and receive…。

grammar.point: 非限定關係子句：which 指前面整件事
grammar.quote: You must be more right than others … which by definition means your thinking has to be different.
grammar.explain:
which 前面的先行詞不是某個名詞，而是整個前一句「你必須比別人更正確」。which means … 的意思是「而這意味著…」。
這種 , which ＋ 動詞 的非限定用法，是補充評論，不是限制範圍。by definition 是插入語。
more right than others 是用 right 的比較級；一般口語會說 more correct，但 Marks 為了強調「對的程度」而刻意使用。
